sections.eyebrow: A party game for phones and a TV
sections.title: Everybody plays, even the narrator
sections.intro: Palermo Noir is the hidden-role game Greeks know as Palermo, a cousin of Mafia and Werewolf. It always needed one friend who sat out: the narrator who knew every secret and counted the votes. Here the game takes that job. Every phone holds its player's secret card, the TV shows the town square, and a deep noir voice runs every night and every day, in English or Greek.

sections.title: One phone each, one TV for the room
sections.intro: You need 6 to 14 players, a phone each, and a screen the whole room can see: a smart TV's browser or a laptop on the TV. Nobody installs anything.

art.alt: Six players lean over a café table in a Palermo piazza at night: role cards dealt face down, a candle, an espresso, a black rose and a ballot box, the known killer lighting a match, the doctor, the police officer, the mayor, the lawyer and the madman with his mask, drawn in gold engraved lines on navy

blocks.text: Each of you has a role. Press and hold your card to see it… and show it to no one.

items: Open a room. The host opens Palermo Noir on their phone and taps Create a room.
Put the town on the TV. Open vgraphics.gr/tv in the TV's browser and type the room code. Friends scan the QR code on the screen to join.
Choose the rules. Classic, Quick or Full house, or your own: the host picks the roles and the timers, and the TV shows the roles in play.
Hold to see your card. Everyone gets a secret role. Your card shows only while you hold it, and every card has the same frame.

sections.title: The town sleeps, two taps each
sections.intro: The TV goes dark and the narrator sends the town to sleep. Every phone asks for two taps: your role's move, or who you trust, then who you suspect. So every phone looks the same, and nobody can tell who did what. On the first night the killers only meet each other and the Police Officer learns the Known Killer's face; from the second night the killers choose a victim.

art.alt: A man in a fedora lights a match on a rooftop terrace above the sleeping city of Palermo: domes, bell towers and a thousand windows down to the harbour, the moon behind thin clouds, a cat on a chimney, in gold engraved lines on navy

blocks.text: The town is whispering. Which name do you hear?

sections.title: Accuse, argue, vote
sections.intro: At dawn the narrator tells the town who the killers found, or that the night passed without a murder, and the TV shows the town's rumour: the most suspected name. Then the room argues, and votes someone out of town.

art.alt: Six suspects stand apart around a lit street lamp in a Palermo piazza at midnight, eyeing each other: the man lighting a match, the doctor, the police officer, the madman on the fountain, the mayor and the lawyer, a black rose on a playing card on the cobbles

blocks.text: Talk. The killer is among you… and listening.

items.title: The accusation board
items.text: Point at a suspect from your phone; the arrows and counts show live on the TV.

items.title: Open or secret votes
items.text: Watch every vote arrive as an arrow, or keep the ballots secret until the end.

items.title: Ties and last words
items.text: Tied players defend themselves and the town votes again. Whoever goes out may say a few last words.

items.title: The night announcer
items.text: The first player out sees every role from then on and tells the dawns, as Greek groups always did.

sections.title: The truth comes out
sections.intro: The game ends the moment one side has won: the town when every killer is out, the killers when they match everyone else, the Madman alone if the town votes him out. Then the TV tells the whole story, and everyone stays in the room to play again.

art.alt: A shaft of light falls on an empty chair with a black rose on its seat in the middle of a Palermo piazza at night, the six characters standing around it between two lit street lamps, the cathedral behind like a stage set

blocks.text: The last killer has fallen. Palermo can finally sleep in peace. The town wins!

items.title: Every card turned
items.text: One by one, killers last, then the winners' banner.

items.title: The story of every night
items.text: Who the killers chose, who the Doctor saved, and who voted whom, secret votes included.

items.title: Awards
items.text: The sharpest eye, the best liar, the lifesaver and the survivor.

items.title: XP and achievements
items.text: Every game counts on your VHub profile, in every VGraphics game.

sections.title: Every role in the deck
sections.intro: The classic roles are in every game: the Known and the Hidden Killer, the Police Officer, the Doctor and the citizens. The extras unlock as a host plays, or all at once for groups who know Palermo. Scroll the deck.

image.alt: The Known Killer's card: a man in a dark overcoat and a fedora lights a match, a rose pinned to his lapel

items.title: Known Killer
items.text: Every night you and your partners choose a victim. The Police Officer knows who you are.
items.back:
You and your partners meet on the first night. From the second night you choose a victim together: the player most of you pick is found at dawn, unless the Doctor protected them.

The Police Officer learns your face on the first night, so stay calm when the town looks your way. The killers win when they equal or outnumber everyone else.

image.alt: The Hidden Killer's card: a slim figure in a long coat, a fedora pulled low over the face, a rose on the lapel

items.title: Hidden Killer
items.text: Every night you and your partners choose a victim. The Police Officer doesn't know you.
items.back:
You meet your partners on the first night, but the Police Officer never learns who you are, and by default the Detective sees you as not a killer.

Choose the victim with your partners every night from the second, and win with them when the killers equal or outnumber the rest.

image.alt: The Police Officer's card: an officer in a peaked cap and a buttoned uniform, writing in a notebook

items.title: Police Officer
items.text: On the first night you learn who the Known Killer is. Steer the town without giving yourself away.
items.back:
On the first night, while the Known Killer raises a hand, you see him. That's your only power.

Steer the town's votes toward him without giving yourself away: the killers will hunt for you. In some groups the host makes your death a win for the killers.

image.alt: The Doctor's card: a woman in a long coat with a stethoscope and a leather doctor's bag

items.title: Doctor
items.text: From the second night, protect one player from the killers, never the same one two nights running.
items.back:
Each night from the second, protect one player. If the killers choose them, the night passes without a murder.

You can't protect the same player two nights running, and by default you may save yourself once a game.

image.alt: A Citizen's card: a smiling baker in an apron with a basket of bread

items.title: Citizen
items.text: No power: listen, accuse, and vote the killers out. Citizens come as a baker, a fisherman, a seamstress and a kiosk owner.
items.back:
No night power. At night you answer who you trust and who you suspect, like everyone else, so your phone looks the same as the rest.

By day you listen, accuse and vote the killers out. Citizens come as a baker, a fisherman, a seamstress and a kiosk owner.

image.alt: The Detective's card: a tall detective in a trench coat and fedora with a pipe and a magnifying glass

items.title: Detective
items.text: Each night, check one player: killer or not.
items.back:
Each night, check one player: your phone answers "killer" or "not a killer" at once.

The Henchman and the Kamikaze show as not a killer, and so does the Hidden Killer unless the host turns that off.

image.alt: The Seer's card: a fortune teller in a patterned headscarf holding a fan of tarot cards

items.title: Seer
items.text: Once a game, at night, learn one player's exact role.
items.back:
Once a game, at night, learn one player's exact role. Pick your night well, or answer "not tonight".

What you learn is yours alone: share it by day, or keep it until it matters.

image.alt: The Bulletproof card: a relieved man in a waistcoat holding up a dented pocket watch

items.title: Bulletproof
items.text: You survive the killers' first attack on you, and only you are told.
items.back:
The first time the killers choose you, you survive. Only you are told; the dawn simply says the night passed without a murder.

After that you're as mortal as anyone, so use what you've learned.

image.alt: The Henchman's card: a young man in braces and a cap, a matchstick in his mouth, twirling a car key

items.title: Henchman
items.text: You know the killers, but they don't know you. You win with them.
items.back:
You know who the killers are, but they don't know you. You don't kill, yet you win with them.

The Detective sees you as not a killer, and in the killers' head count you count as a townsperson.

image.alt: The Mayor's card: a stout mayor with a curled moustache, a sash and a ceremonial key

items.title: Mayor
items.text: Reveal yourself during a day: from then on your vote counts twice.
items.back:
Keep your role secret until the right moment, then tap Reveal during a day.

From then on a gold badge shows on your tile, everyone knows who you are, and your vote counts twice.

image.alt: The Hunter's card: a countryman in a flat cap and tweed with a hunting horn, his hound at his feet

items.title: Hunter
items.text: When you're out, by vote or by night, you take one player with you.
items.back:
When you go out, by the vote, by night or by a bomb, you have 20 seconds to take one player with you.

Take a killer and the town cheers; take a friend and you'll hear about it.

image.alt: The Lawyer's card: a lawyer in a pinstriped suit and round spectacles, a briefcase in one hand, one finger raised

items.title: Lawyer
items.text: You're dealt 5 of 17 power cards, such as Objection!, Alibi and Appeal, and keep 2. Each one works once.
items.back:
At the start you're dealt 5 of the 17 power cards in the briefcase and keep 2, such as Objection!, Alibi or Appeal.

Each card works once, at its own moment: at night, in the talk, at the vote or at a verdict. The TV shows when the Lawyer steps in, never who.

image.alt: The Kamikaze's card: a grinning man in a striped shirt holding up a round cartoon bomb with a sparkling fuse

items.title: Kamikaze
items.text: You're with the killers. Once, during a day, you can take one player down with you.
items.back:
You're with the killers, and they know you.

Once, during a day's discussion, hold Explode and pick a player: both of you fall at once, with a bang on the TV.

image.alt: The Madman's card: a man in a rumpled suit with wild hair, holding a cracked harlequin mask

items.title: Madman
items.text: You win alone if the town votes you out, and that ends the game.
items.back:
You win alone if the town votes you out, and that ends the game on the spot, to your tarantella.

Killed at night, you just die. So act suspicious, but not too suspicious.

sections.title: Listen to the soundtrack
sections.intro: The music of an evening in Palermo, in the order you hear it: a 1950s Sicilian noir chamber orchestra with staccato strings, clarinet, mandolin and accordion. Hushed for the night, sunny but suspicious at noon, relentless for the vote, and a theme for whoever wins. Press play and keep reading; a small player stays with you down the page.

cover.alt: The Palermo Noir soundtrack cover: a shaft of light on an empty chair with a black rose, in a Palermo piazza at night before the cathedral, in gold engraved lines on navy

sections.eyebrow: Why your group will love it
sections.title: A night out, without leaving the sofa

items.title: Everybody plays
items.text: The game deals the cards, runs the nights, counts the votes and keeps the rules, so nobody sits out to narrate.

items.title: A noir narrator
items.text: A deep voice on the TV tells every night and every dawn. It never says a name: the names are on the screen.

items.title: No secret leaks
items.text: Every phone shows the same screens and asks for the same taps at night, and your card shows only while you hold it.

items.title: Any TV, nothing to install
items.text: A smart TV's browser or a laptop on the TV, and the phones you already have.

items.title: English or Greek
items.text: The narrator, the cards and every screen, in the host's language.

items.title: Free, every role
items.text: Up to 14 players with every role in. Ads only between games, never during one.

band.title: For ages 13 and up
band.text: Each phone gives its year of birth once, and only an age group is kept, never the year. Players join as a guest or with their VHub name, and the TV signs in as a screen, never as a person.
